capitalismdebates.intro: This entry joins several distinct controversies. Compare selected books on corporate finance, slavery and abolition, cotton, and global divergence.
capitalismdebates.question: Which books appear in which regional and degree cohorts? Read their arguments and the recorded critiques alongside their citation patterns.
capitalismdebates.observation: Williams’s Capitalism and Slavery appears in 56 sampled dissertations and Drescher’s Econocide in 21. Read the entry’s account of their disagreement alongside these counts; citation presence cannot show which argument a dissertation adopts.

existing_anchor: Richard White and Railroaded were already verified in revisions1.157–1.159; preserve the inherited-d and namesake qualification.
selection_limits: Eight new selected bridges, not all economic-history scholars. Existing search thresholds (works >=20 dated dissertations, people >=30) are preserved. Fogel, Wrigley, Mokyr, de Vries and Brenner have searchable person records but the selected works inspected do not meet the public work threshold; they are not treated as uncited. Field panels are editorial selections from existing rosters, not field-readership aggregates. Counts overlap and must not be added. No causal influence is inferred.
protected: No changes to graph IDs, edges, chronologies, source-reading qualifications, citation records or identity splits; OpenAlex remains paused.
observation_basis: Field observations use the exact selected work counts/region totals in the frozen public source buckets. The Williams/Drescher disagreement is already documented in the capitalismdebates roster and sources; no new book-body interpretation is asserted.
